theater: 江都顯福宮（江蘇揚州東北）

battle.name: 顯福宮之戰
battle.theater: 江都顯福宮（江蘇揚州東北）
battle.brief: 大業十四年三月，宇文化及弒隋煬帝於江都，率眾十餘萬溯江北上，行至顯福宮。虎賁郎將麥孟才、虎牙郎將錢傑與折衝郎將沈光糾合數千人，謀晨發襲殺化及，事洩後化及夜出營外，司馬德戡引兵圍攻，沈光以下數百人戰死不降。卡面科林斯青銅盔未見於此役，隋軍兜鍪與之同屬全覆面護頭一路。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 大業十四年（618）三月江都的分裂，表面是一場宮廷政變，實際是一支十餘萬人的隋軍縱隊在行軍途中裂成兩半。宇文化及一方：自稱大丞相、總百揆，接手了他自己用兵變奪來的隋朝中央——江都留守的宿衛、禁中給使、關中驍果，以及從江都民間強奪來的舟楫；名義上他仍立秦王浩為帝居別宮，以中宮名義發詔畫敕，百官照舊參朝，因此這一方的名號仍是「隋」。兵權分配零碎：宿衛交給虎賁郎將司馬德戡與元禮，直閣裴虔通主殿內，鷹揚郎將孟秉與將作少監宇文智及在城外集兵，折衝郎將沈光領給使營宿於禁內，江都城防由城門郎唐奉義閉鎖。反對一方沒有正式名號與編制：麥孟才、錢傑、沈光三人所代表的是受隋煬帝厚恩的宿衛將佐，麥孟才以虎賁郎將身分糾合恩舊、帥所將數千人，打算在晨起啟程時一擊而誅宇文化及；這支部隊只靠營帳之間的私約與舊誼維繫，沒有可以公開的旗號，計畫一洩便無從挽回。地理上，兩方同處一個北上的水陸行軍縱隊之中：化及的中軍、帳幕、六宮與內侍在營心，士卒營帳沿岸排開，宿衛、給使與將士混編一處，任何一方的異動都會被另一方立刻看見。這不是兩軍對壘的會戰，而是一場宿營之中的近身格鬥。
countriesEn: The split that tore Jiangdu apart in the third month of Daye 14 (618) looked like a palace coup, but it was in fact a column of more than a hundred thousand men of the Sui army breaking in two on the march. On the side of Yuwen Huaji stood the chancellor who had taken the Sui state over by force of arms: the garrison left at Jiangdu, the attendants of the forbidden quarters, the picked Xianbei-guards from Guanzhong, and the boats seized from the people of Jiangdu. In name he still set Qin Wang Hao up as emperor in a separate palace, issued writs in the name of the empress, and the officers of court went on attending as before, so that this side still bore the name of Sui. The command was fragmented: the palace guard was given to the tiger-guard commander Sima Dekan and to Yuan Li, the chamberlain Pei Qiantong held the inner hall, the eagle-guard commander Meng Bing and the deputy director of imperial works Yuwen Zhiji gathered men outside the walls, the dashing officer Shen Guang was made to command the attendants' camp inside the forbidden quarters, and the city gates were locked by the gate officer Tang Fengyi. The other side had no name and no establishment. What Mc Mengcai, Qian Jie and Shen Guang represented was the Sui's own trusted officers, men who had received great kindness from Emperor Yang. Mc Mengcai, a tiger-guard commander, gathered his old associates and led the several thousand men under him, meaning to strike Yuwen Huaji down the moment the column set out at dawn; this body was held together only by private oaths passed between tents and by old ties of comradeship, with no banner it could fly in the open and no way to recover once the plot leaked. Geographically the two sides stood inside one marching column travelling north by water: Huaji's centre, his tent, the six palaces and the eunuchs lay at the heart of the camp, the soldiers' tents were strung out along the bank, the guard, the attendants and the rank and file were quartered together, and any move by one side was visible to the other at once. This was not a battle between two armies but a close-quarters struggle inside a camp.
people: 全場關鍵人物集中在十數人身上。宇文化及是那場弒君的主謀：右屯衛將軍出身，性駑怯，聞謀反時變色流汗，被弟弟宇文智及與司馬德戡等推上前；殺隋煬帝後自稱大丞相、總百揆，把六宮改作自己的御宮，營前另立帳、仗衛部伍皆擬乘輿，自奉養一如煬帝，而正是這份仿照舊主的排場，激起宿衛的舊恨。司馬德戡，扶風人，虎賁郎將，受煬帝寵信而領驍果屯於東城，是三月十五日夜兵變的發動者：他在東城集兵數萬人、舉火與城外相應，又奉命鎮壓顯福宮之亂，殺沈光、圍殲其麾下數百人；事後以功封溫國公、加光祿大夫，數日內卻被改任禮部尚書而奪去兵柄，憤怨之下密謀以後軍萬餘人襲殺化及，事發被擒，遭縊殺，支黨十餘人同死。沈光是此役另一位主角：折衝郎將，以驍勇聞名，被化及派去領給使營宿於禁內；聽到麥孟才的密謀，他哭著說「是所望於將軍也」，事洩後率眾突襲化及本營卻撲空，被德戡入圍，麾下數百人全部死戰、無一人降。麥孟才，虎賁郎將，是隋朝名將麥鐵杖之子，由他糾合恩舊、帥數千人發動這次襲擊，事敗被斬；錢傑，虎牙郎將，與麥、沈同謀，《資治通鑑》未載其下落。江都兵變的其餘骨幹——裴虔通、元禮、令狐行達、馬文舉、封德彝、宇文智及、許弘仁、張愷、唐奉義、牛方裕、薛世良、孟秉、趙行樞、元敏——在同一夜完成了弒君與改立傀儡的全套動作；而被推上前台的秦王浩，成年後仍只是這場權力交易的傀儡。
peopleEn: The decisive actors were a dozen-odd men. Yuwen Huaji was the author of the regicide: a man of the Right Garrison, timid by nature, who turned pale and sweated when the plot was put to him, and who was pushed to the front by his brother Yuwen Zhiji and by Sima Dekan and the rest. After killing Emperor Yang he called himself chancellor and took over all affairs, turned the six palaces into his own imperial quarters, set up a separate tent before the camp with his guards and ranks dressed in the ceremonial of the imperial carriage, and kept himself in the style of Emperor Yang; and it was precisely that borrowed splendour that stirred the old resentment in the guard. Sima Dekan, a native of Fufeng and commander of the tiger guards, was trusted by Yang Guang and commanded the picked troops in the east of the city; he was the man who set the coup of the fifteenth night in motion, massing several tens of thousands in the east of the city and raising fires to answer those outside, and he was the one who was then ordered to put down the rising at Xianfu Palace, killing Shen Guang and encircling several hundred of his men. Rewarded for it, he was made Duke of Wen and given the additional office of Grand Master of Ceremonies, and within days was shifted to the Ministry of Rites to strip him of his command; bitter at this he plotted to kill Huaji with more than ten thousand men of the rear army, was discovered, was bound and hanged, and a dozen of his confederates died with him. Shen Guang was the other central figure of the affair: a dashing officer, famed for valour, whom Huaji set to command the attendants' camp inside the forbidden quarters. Hearing Mc Mengcai's plan he wept and said that this was what he had hoped for from his general; when the plot leaked he led his men against Huaji's own tent, found it empty, was enclosed by Dekan, and every one of the several hundred under him fought to the death with not a man surrendering. Mc Mengcai, a tiger-guard commander and son of the Sui general Mai Tiezhang, was the man who gathered the old associates and led the several thousand in the attack, and was beheaded when it failed; Qian Jie, a tiger-fang officer, shared the plot, and the Zizhi Tongjian records nothing further of his fate. The rest of the backbone of the Jiangdu coup — Pei Qiantong, Yuan Li, Linghu Xingda, Ma Wenju, Feng Deyi, Yuwen Zhiji, Xu Hongren, Zhang Kai, Tang Fengyi, Niu Fangyu, Xue Shiliang, Meng Bing, Zhao Xingshu and Yuan Min — carried out the whole sequence of regicide and puppet installation in a single night; and Qin Wang Hao, whom they set on the throne, remained for the rest of his life a puppet of that transaction.
kits: 卡面這頂科林斯青銅盔（Corinthian helmet）並沒有出現在顯福宮，也不會戴在任何一名隋軍的頭上：它約在公元前650年前後定型，是希臘城邦重裝步兵（hoplite）用一整片青銅打出的全覆面頭盔，兩側只留狹長眼孔，中央一道鼻樑，連頸肩都由同一片金屬包住。把它放進這場戰役的裝備表，是因為它代表護頭技術的一條老路——用金屬把整個頭面包住——而這條路在中國走的是另一個分支：隋軍的兜鍪與冑。隋代兜鍪多以皮胎為胎，外覆鐵葉或青銅葉，脊線隆起，兩側加護耳，頸後垂披膊；它比科林斯盔輕得多，工料也簡陋得多，不開眼孔，靠護耳與披膊擋住側面的斬擊與流矢。與兜鍪配套的是甲身：隋承漢魏之制，明光鎧的形制仍在使用，甲片以皮條綴連，肩吞與臂鎧護住上身；卡面科林斯盔那種「一體成形、把人整個罩住」的思路，在隋代是由披膊加護肩分別完成的。此役真正的近戰兵器是長刀與槊：折衝郎將沈光所屬的近衛以刀槊衝撞見長，隋軍通用橫刀（雙刃，可斬可刺）與長槊，弓弩則是遠程主力，江都宿衛與驍果皆善射。舟師方面，這支部隊靠的是江都與彭城水路的船隻，五牙大艦與鬥艦為骨幹，舳艫相接、帆檣蔽江，連同運載什物與舟子的舟船，數以千計；軍資則以人力背負，戈甲戎器悉令軍士負之，長途北行時人人自負甲兵，這正是軍怨的來源。糧食方面，江都早已糧盡，化及北行只能靠沿途徵發與強奪民船民車牛，甚至連車輛都掠去二千輛。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card did not appear at Xianfu Palace, and it would not have been worn by any man of the Sui army. It took shape around 650 BC, and it was a fully enclosing bronze helmet made by Greek citizen hoplites from a single sheet of metal, with narrow eye openings cut to either side, a central nasal, and the neck and shoulders covered by the same sheet. It belongs in the equipment table of this battle because it represents one old line in the history of head protection, the line of wrapping the whole head in metal, and the line that in China ran through a different branch: the Sui dou kou and zhou. The Sui helmet was built on a leather core covered with sheets of iron or bronze, with a raised ridge, cheek pieces at the sides and a neck curtain at the back. It was far lighter and far cruder than the Corinthian shell, it had no eye openings at all, and it met a cutting stroke or a stray arrow with cheek piece and neck curtain. The body armour went with it: the Sui inherited the forms of the Han and Wei, the ming guang jia of the northern plains was still worn, plates were laced together with leather thongs, and shoulder and arm pieces covered the upper body. The idea of the Corinthian shell, of one piece of metal enclosing the whole man, was in the Sui achieved in parts instead, by a neck curtain and shoulder guards put together. The weapons that really mattered at Xianfu Palace were the long dao and the shao: the close guard of the dashing officer Shen Guang was strong in charging with blade and spear, the common Sui arm was the heng dao, a double-edged sword fit to cut and to thrust, and with the shao, while the bow and the crossbow were the ranged arm, and the garrison and the picked troops of Jiangdu were all good at the bow. On the water this column depended on the craft of the Jiangdu and Pengcheng waterways, with five-toothed and fighting towers as its backbone, decks chained one to another and sails and masts covering the river, and the humble boats that carried stores and boatmen numbered in the thousands. Stores were carried on men's backs, the armour and weapons and kit of the whole army were all loaded onto the soldiers themselves, and on a long march north every man carried his own harness: that was the source of the resentment in the ranks. As for food, Jiangdu had long been out of grain, and Huaji could only live on requisitions along the line and on boats and draught animals seized from the people, taking two thousand carts as well.
tactics: 這場衝突本質上是一次宿營中的刺殺計畫失敗，戰術全在夜與晨之間。宇文化及一方在三月十五日夜已展示過一次成功的夜襲：司馬德戡在東城集兵數萬人、舉火與城外相應，裴虔通以直閣之權接管玄武門宿衛，諸門皆不下鑰，三更發動，天未明即控制成象殿與永巷。顯福宮的計畫則是把這套夜襲經驗反過來用在宇文化及身上：麥孟才糾合恩舊數千人，約定在「晨起將發時」動手——全軍拔營啟程、帳幕拆撤、戒嚴交接的那一刻，正是防備最薄、標的最多之時；其設想是一擊而擒，或至少迫化及退讓，再轉而號召全軍。計畫走漏後，宇文化及採取的應對不是死守而是有意離營：他與腹心連夜走出營外，只留人告知司馬德戡等討伐，等於把攻擊目標從自己身上移走，同時把報復交給武裝力量。於是沈光聽到營內喧譖，知事情已發，便率眾直撲化及本營，營中已空，途中只遇內史侍郎元敏，被斬；德戡隨即引兵入圍，切斷其退路，沈光以下數百人全部死戰、無一降者，麥孟才亦死。整個過程的次序很清楚：先奪標的，再封退路，後掃殘部；行軍縱隊中營與營之間的距離被壓到極短，使整座營地變成口袋。餘波同樣慘烈：化及北上的計劃因內部流血而崩壞，士卒怨言日起；而鎮壓有功的司馬德戡數日後被奪去兵柄，以後軍萬餘人再圖反制，說明這支部隊的忠是靠不住的。
tacticsEn: The clash was in essence a plan to stab an enemy inside his camp, and the whole of the tactic lay between nightfall and dawn. Yuwen Huaji's side had already shown one night attack working three weeks earlier: Sima Dekan massed several tens of thousands in the east of the city and raised fires to answer those outside, the chamberlain Pei Qiantong took over the guard at Xuanwu Gate with the authority of his office, none of the gates was locked, the move began in the third watch, and before dawn the palace halls of Chengxiang and the Yong lane were in their hands. The plan at Xianfu Palace turned that lesson round and used it on Yuwen Huaji himself. Mc Mengcai gathered his old associates, several thousand men, and fixed the moment for the attack on the hour when the column would set out at dawn, when the tents were being struck and the watch was being handed over: that was the thinnest moment of defence and the moment when there were most targets. The idea was to take him by one blow, or at least drive him back and then rally the whole army. Once the plot leaked, Huaji's answer was not to stand and fight but deliberately to leave the camp: he went out of it in the night with his closest men, left word with Sima Dekan and the others to go and punish the rebels, and so he moved the target off his own person and handed the business to armed men. Shen Guang heard the uproar in the camp, knew the affair was discovered, and led his men straight at Huaji's tent, which was empty; on the way he ran into the Interior Secretary Yuan Min and cut him down. Dekan then led his troops in and surrounded them, cutting off the retreat, and every one of the several hundred under Shen Guang fought to the death and not a man surrendered; Mc Mengcai died as well. The order of the whole thing is plain. First the target was taken, then the retreat was closed, then the remnants were swept up; the distance between camp and camp in a marching column was short enough to turn the whole encampment into a pocket. The aftermath was no less brutal: Huaji's plan to march north was broken by the bleeding inside his own ranks and muttering grew among the soldiers; and Dekan, who had distinguished himself in the suppression, was stripped of his command a few days later and moved to raise more than ten thousand men of the rear army against Huaji, which shows how unreliable the loyalty of this column was.
data: 可核對的數字都出自《資治通鑑》卷一百八十五。時間：隋大業十四年三月丙辰（618年3月15日）夜江都兵變，隋煬帝被縊；顯福宮之戰緊接其後，同在三月，發生在北上的行軍途中。兵員：三月十五日夜，司馬德戡在東城集兵「數萬人」；弒君之後，宇文化及「擁眾十餘萬」，並「據有六宮」。叛方人數：麥孟才「糾合恩舊，帥所將數千人」。損失：沈光被殺，「其麾下數百人皆鬥死，一無降者」；麥孟才亦死。相關數字：化及北行至彭城，因水路不通，強奪民車牛「二千輛」以載宮人珍寶，戈甲戎器悉令軍士負之；與此役同時，沈法興在吳興起兵討化及，至烏程得精卒六萬，據江表十郡；北方的李密乘勝擁兵三十餘萬，陳於北邙。需要打折的推估：所謂十餘萬眾包含大量被強徵的江都民夫、舟子與從駕驍果，戰鬥力遠低於編制數；麥孟才部的數千人分佈在多座營帳，能同時投入突擊者有限；此役是營內政變，雙方實際接戰的兵力以千計而非以萬計。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked all come from volume one hundred and eighty-five of the Zizhi Tongjian. Timing: on the night of the bing chen day, the third month of Daye 14, that is 15 March 618, the coup at Jiangdu took place and Emperor Yang was hanged; the fighting at Xianfu Palace followed at once, in the same month, on the march north. Numbers: on the night of the fifteenth, Sima Dekan massed several tens of thousands in the east of the city; after the regicide Yuwen Huaji had more than a hundred thousand men with him and held the six palaces. The rebels: Mc Mengcai gathered his old associates and led several thousand of the men under him. Losses: Shen Guang was killed and every one of the several hundred under him fought to the death, with not one surrendering; Mc Mengcai also died. Related figures: when Huaji reached Pengcheng the water route was blocked, and he took two thousand carts and draught animals from the people to carry the palace women and treasure, while the armour, weapons and kit of the army were all loaded on the soldiers; at the same time as this battle Shen Faxing rose in Wuxing to punish Huaji, reached Wuchun with sixty thousand picked troops and took ten commanderies of Jiangnan; and in the north Li Mi, riding high after his victory, drew up more than three hundred thousand men before Beiming. Estimates that must be discounted: the hundred thousand men included a large number of Jiangdu labour levy, boatmen and picked guards who had come with the emperor, and their fighting worth was far below the figure on paper; the several thousand of Mc Mengcai were spread over several camps and only part of them could be committed to the attack at one moment; and this was a rising inside a camp, so the forces actually engaged on both sides are to be counted in thousands, not in tens of thousands.
cause: 打起來有四層原因。第一層是江都的困局：隋煬帝自大業元年起屢次南巡，最後駐扎江都不肯北還，宮中設百餘房、從姬千餘人，江都糧盡，從駕驍果多關中人，久客思鄉，叛意早種；郎將竇賢曾率所部西走被追斬，逃亡者仍不止其數。三月十五日夜，司馬德戡、裴虔通、宇文智及等以驍果為主力發動兵變，當夜弒君。第二層是化及奪權後的失度：他自稱大丞相、總百揆，以秦王浩為帝居別宮，奪江都人舟楫，又把六宮依舊式改作御宮、營前另立帳、仗衛部伍皆擬乘輿，自奉養一如煬帝，內外戒嚴之際卻聲稱要回長安。一支十餘萬人的隊伍被這樣一位主人帶著，士氣只能往下掉。第三層是軍隊的忠誠結構：沈光原為隋朝折衝郎將，被化及用來領給使營宿於禁內，等於讓舊朝將領看守弒君者的宮禁；麥孟才、錢傑則是受先帝厚恩的宿衛，「吾儕受先帝厚恩，今俯首事仇，受其驅帥，何面目視息世間哉」——這句話就是這場衝突的直接動機：所爭的不是地盤，而是不肯對殺主者俯首。第四層是時機與空間：北上的長隊宿營在岸，帳幕相連、晨起啟程，正是全營注意力最集中而戒備最鬆的一刻，麥孟才選的正是這個窗口。事敗之後，仇恨並未消散，反倒因鎮壓而更加集結，這就是德戡其後再舉事的土壤。
causeEn: There were four layers of reason. The first was the trap Jiangdu had become. Since the first year of Daye Emperor Yang had gone south again and again, and at the end he sat at Jiangdu and would not go north; the palace had a hundred rooms and more than a thousand concubines, the city was out of grain, and the picked guards who had come with the emperor were mostly men from Guanzhong, long away from home and sick to return. The lieutenant Dou Xian once led his men west and was run down and killed, and others kept slipping away. On the night of the fifteenth of March, Sima Dekan, Pei Qiantong, Yuwen Zhiji and the rest moved against the emperor with the picked troops as their main strength, and the regicide was done that night. The second layer was how badly Huaji ruled once he had the power. He called himself chancellor and took over all affairs, set Qin Wang Hao up as emperor in a separate palace, took the boats of the people of Jiangdu, converted the six palaces into imperial quarters in the old style, raised a separate tent before the camp with his guards and ranks dressed in the ceremonial of the imperial carriage, and kept himself in the manner of Emperor Yang; while a city was under martial law he announced that he was going back to Chang'an. A column of more than a hundred thousand men led by such a man could only lose heart. The third layer was how loyalty was distributed inside the army. Shen Guang had been a dashing officer of the Sui, and Huaji set him to command the attendants' camp inside the forbidden quarters, which is to say he posted a general of the old dynasty to guard the palace of the man who had killed his emperor; Mc Mengcai and Qian Jie were guards who owed the former emperor great kindness, and their words are the direct motive of the whole affair: we received great kindness from the late emperor; now we bow before our enemy and take his orders; how can we look the world in the face and go on living. What was at stake was not territory but the refusal to bow to a regicide. The fourth layer was timing and space. The long column going north was camped on the bank, tent joined to tent, and the hour of setting out in the morning was the moment when the whole camp's attention was most concentrated and its guard at its weakest; that was the window Mc Mengcai chose. And after the failure the hatred did not die down: the suppression only gathered it closer together, which is the soil in which Dekan's later rising grew.
impact: 這一戰的影響不在戰果，而在它暴露的東西。第一，它把隋朝最後的武力底子——宿衛、禁中給使、關中驍果——的忠誠狀態一次攤開：同一批人，數日前才替化及殺了皇帝，數日後又反過來要殺化及；鎮壓成功的司馬德戡被封溫國公、加光祿大夫，數日後改任禮部尚書而奪兵柄，憤怨之下企圖以後軍萬餘人襲殺化及，連同支黨十餘人被誅。可見隋末的暴力不是單點爆發，而是連鎖式的，宮禁與軍隊之間已無可靠紐帶，這正是隋朝迅速崩解的內部原因。第二，它打斷了宇文化及的北上計劃，也間接改變了江南與北方的權力版圖：化及自江都帶走舟楫、器械與大批物資往北，令江表諸郡另立旗號，沈法興據江表十郡，蕭銑都江陵、擁兵四十餘萬，李襲志守交州；而李密乘勝在洛北擊潰王世充、擁兵三十餘萬陳於北邙，逼近東都。若化及能順利北還收拾關中，隋末最後的南北樞紐便不會在這個春天斷掉。第三，它在制度上留下兩樣痕跡：一是宿衛與給使分屬兩套體系、人數與任務都很小的近衛編制，後來唐代北衙禁軍的某些要素可以從此役的編制痕跡裡看出端倪；二是「宿營之內、刀兵未發而內亂先起」的教訓，歷代講兵事與講忠誠，都拿沈光「是所望於將軍也」與麾下數百人「無一降者」作例子。
impactEn: The significance of this fight does not lie in its results but in what it laid bare. First, it spread out the state of the loyalty of the last military resources of the Sui, the palace guard, the attendants of the forbidden quarters and the picked troops from Guanzhong. The same men who a few days earlier had killed the emperor on Huaji's behalf turned a few days later against Huaji himself; and Sima Dekan, who had succeeded in the suppression and was made Duke of Wen and Grand Master of Ceremonies, was shifted to the Ministry of Rites a few days later to take away his command, and in his bitterness plotted to kill Huaji with more than ten thousand men of the rear army, he and a dozen of his confederates being killed. The violence of late Sui was therefore not a single eruption but a chain reaction, and between the palace and the army there was no sound bond left: that was the inner reason the Sui fell apart so quickly. Second, it broke up Huaji's plan to march north and so changed the balance of power in the south and the north. Huaji carried the boats, the equipment and a great deal of goods away from Jiangdu to the north, which left the commanderies of Jiangnan to raise banners of their own: Shen Faxing held ten commanderies of Jiangnan, Xiao Xian moved his capital to Jiangling with more than four hundred thousand men, Li Xizhi held Jiaozhou; and in the north Li Mi, riding on his victory, routed Wang Shichong north of Luoyang and drew up more than three hundred thousand men before Beiming, pressing on the eastern capital. Had Huaji got north in good order and taken over what remained of Guanzhong, the last hinge joining north and south in late Sui would not have snapped in that spring. Third, it left two traces in institutions. One is the division of the guard and the attendants into two separate systems, a close guard of very small numbers with very small tasks, out of which certain elements of the Tang northern palace guard can be traced; the other is the lesson of a mutiny breaking out inside a camp before a blow is struck, and in later ages, when men wrote about war and about loyalty, they used Shen Guang's words, this is what I hoped for from my general, and the several hundred under him of whom not one surrendered, as their example.
result: 結局是反方全敗，宇文化及完勝，但代價記在帳上。顯福宮一戰：沈光被司馬德戡所殺，其麾下數百人全部鬥死、無一人降，麥孟才被斬首，錢傑的下落史無明文；宇文化及在事發之前已與腹心走出營外，標的倖免，卻也從此對自己的宿衛再無信任。隨後的連鎖反應更緊：鎮壓有功的司馬德戡受封溫國公、加光祿大夫，數日後被改任禮部尚書而奪去兵柄，憤怨之下謀以後軍萬餘人襲殺化及，事發被擒，遭縊殺，支黨十餘人同誅；化及北上的軍隊則因士卒自負甲兵、連日勞苦而怨言叢生，至彭城水路不通，還要強奪民車牛二千輛以載宮人珍寶，士氣崩落。化及本人在江都的統治也未能維持多久：武德二年（619）王世充乘其內部混亂進攻江都，化及兵敗退保黃河以北，後為竇建德所迎；武德五年（622）竇建德敗亡時化及亦被擒送京，此後數年才被處決。總的來說：這場戰役以「弒君者差點被自己人殺掉」收場，短兵相接的宿衛格鬥以守方全勝告終，但它同時標誌著一支本已崩解的軍隊，連同它所承載的王朝，進入了無休止的內耗循環。
resultEn: The rebels were utterly defeated and Yuwen Huaji won, but the cost was booked against him. In the fighting at Xianfu Palace, Shen Guang was killed by Sima Dekan, every one of the several hundred under him fought to the death and not one surrendered, Mc Mengcai was beheaded, and the Zizhi Tongjian says nothing more of the fate of Qian Jie. Huaji had already left the camp with his closest men before the move began, so the target escaped, but from that day he never again trusted his own guard. The chain reaction that followed was even tighter. Sima Dekan, who had distinguished himself in the suppression, was made Duke of Wen and given the additional office of Grand Master of Ceremonies, and within days was shifted to the Ministry of Rites to strip him of his command; in his bitterness he plotted to kill Huaji with more than ten thousand men of the rear army, was taken, was hanged, and a dozen of his confederates were executed with him. The army marching north under Huaji meanwhile began to mutter, since the soldiers carried their own armour and weapons and the days were hard; when it reached Pengcheng and the water route was blocked, two thousand carts and draught animals were taken from the people to carry the palace women and treasure, and the morale of the column collapsed. Huaji's own tenure at Jiangdu was not long either: in the second year of Wude, 619, Wang Shichong took advantage of the confusion inside his camp and attacked Jiangdu, Huaji was beaten and fell back north of the Yellow River, and he was later received by Dou Jiande; when Dou Jiande was destroyed in the fifth year of Wude, 622, Huaji was taken and sent to the capital, and was not put to death until some years afterwards. In sum, this battle ended with the regicide nearly killed by his own men, the close fighting inside the camp going entirely to the defenders, and at the same time marking the entry of an already disintegrating army, together with the dynasty it carried, into an endless cycle of internal consumption.
